'''Onsen-ji''' (温泉寺) is a {{ill|Rinzai school|en|Rinzai school|qid=Q639625|lt=Rinzai}} Buddhist temple affiliated with the [[Myoshin-ji]] branch, located in the city of {{ill|Suwa, Nagano|en|Suwa, Nagano|qid=Q846338|lt=Suwa}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. The temple's mountain name is Rinjozan (臨江山), and its principal deity is [[:en:Yakushi Nyorai|Yakushi Nyorai]] (Bhaisajyaguru). It serves as the 7th station of the [[Chubu 49 Yakushi Pilgrimage]] and the 24th station of the [[Suwa 33 Kannon Pilgrimage]].

== History ==
Onsen-ji was established in {{ill|1640|en|1640|qid=Q6901|lt=1640}} (Kan'ei 17) by the second lord of {{ill|Takamatsu Domain|en|Takamatsu Domain|qid=Q1036915|lt=Takamatsu}}, [[:en:Suwa Tadatsune|Suwa Tadatsune]], to safeguard the {{ill|Onsen|en|Onsen|qid=Q655311|lt=Onsen}} sources of the area. The founding monk, [[Tairei Genmi]], was invited from the [[Jiun-ji Temple|Jiun-ji]] in {{ill|Shimosuwa|ar|شيموسوا|arz|شيموسوا|ceb|Shimosuwa Machi|es|Shimosuwa|fa|شیموسووا، ناگانو|fi|Shimo-Suwa|fr|Shimosuwa|hy|Սիմոսուվա|it|Shimosuwa|ja|下諏訪町|ko|시모스와정|ms|Shimosuwa, Nagano|my|ရှိမိုဆုဝမြို့၊ နဂါနို|pl|Shimosuwa|ru|Симосува|sv|Shimosuwa|tl|Shimosuwa, Nagano|tr|Shimosuwa|uk|Сімо-Сува|ur|شیموسووا|uz|Shimosuva|zh|下諏訪町|qid=Q1204211|lt=Shimosuwa}}. The temple became the family temple of the Suwa clan, with the graves of eight generations of clan heads, from [[:en:Suwa Tadatsune|Suwa Tadatsune]] to {{ill|Suwa Tadamasa|en|Suwa Tadamasa|qid=Q11631883|lt=Suwa Tadamasa}}.

After a fire in 1870 (Meiji 3), which destroyed its main structures, the temple's gates, Noh stage, and Yakui-mon were relocated from {{ill|Takamatsu Castle|en|Takamatsu Castle|qid=Q1305872|lt=Takamatsu Castle}} to reconstruct the temple grounds. The site also features a statue by {{ill|Mokujiki|en|Mokujiki|qid=Q104876072|lt=Mokujiki}}, stone statues by [[Moriya Teiji]], and a bronze bell believed to have been repurposed from the {{ill|Battle of Nagashino|ar|معركة ناغاشينو|azb|ناقاشینو دؤیوشو|ca|Batalla de Nagashino|de|Schlacht von Nagashino|eo|Batalo de Nagashino|es|Batalla de Nagashino|fa|نبرد ناگاشینو|fi|Nagashinon taistelu|fr|Bataille de Nagashino|he|קרב נאגאשינו|id|Pertempuran Nagashino|it|Battaglia di Nagashino|ja|長篠の戦い|ko|나가시노 전투|ms|Pertempuran Nagashino|my|နဂါရှိနိုတိုက်ပွဲ|nl|Slag bij Nagashino|no|Slaget ved Nagashino|pl|Bitwa pod Nagashino|pt|Batalha de Nagashino|ru|Битва при Нагасино|simple|Battle of Nagashino|sr|Битка код Нагашина|th|ยุทธการที่นากาชิโนะ|tr|Nagashino Muharebesi|uk|Битва при Наґасіно|vi|Trận Nagashino|zh|長篠之戰|qid=Q428369|lt=Battle of Nagashino}}.

The temple's location on a hill offers panoramic views of {{ill|Lake Suwa|en|Lake Suwa|qid=Q1206692|lt=Lake Suwa}} and the surrounding hot spring town.

== Cultural Assets ==
* '''National Historic Site''': Takamatsu Clan Graveyard (jointly designated with [[Raigaku-ji]])
* '''Suwa City Cultural Property''': Onsen-ji Iron Pagoda (a multi-storied pagoda used for relics)
* '''City Cultural Property''': The pagoda and Noh stage are both historical assets of regional significance.

== Access ==
Onsen-ji is a 15-minute walk from {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=JR}} {{ill|Chūō Main Line|en|Chūō Main Line|qid=Q1078110|lt=Chūō Main Line}}'s [[Kamisuwa Station]].
